headline: Mirza Fakhrul to take oath as 23rd President Friday evening
summary: The President-elect will visit the graves of Ziaur Rahman and Khaleda Zia before the swearing-in ceremony at Bangabhaban.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir will be sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh on Friday evening at Bangabhaban.
Before the ceremony, he is scheduled to pay respects at the graves of former President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia at Zia Uddyan in Dhaka.
Following the tribute, the President-elect will offer prayers and Fatihah at the memorials.
Mirza Fakhrul was elected by Members of Parliament on Thursday, receiving 255 votes out of a total of 349.
France and Switzerland have already sent congratulations to the new President.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is set to become the 23rd President of Bangladesh.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir will be sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh on Friday evening at Bangabhaban.

Before the ceremony, he is scheduled to pay respects at the graves of former President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia at Zia Uddyan in Dhaka.

Following the tribute, the President-elect will offer prayers and Fatihah at the memorials.

Mirza Fakhrul was elected by Members of Parliament on Thursday, receiving 255 votes out of a total of 349.

France and Switzerland have already sent congratulations to the new President.

headline_marked: Court order: [[Imran Khan moved to hospital]] for medical exam
headline: Court order: Imran Khan moved to hospital for medical exam
summary: The jailed former Pakistani PM was transferred from Adiala Jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad following a Supreme Court mandate.
details: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was transferred from Adiala Jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad early Friday morning for a medical examination.
The move follows a Supreme Court order issued this week, requiring authorities to transfer the 73-year-old former leader within 48 hours.

Khan's party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), and his lawyers claim his health has deteriorated during his imprisonment since August 2023, specifically citing significant vision loss in his right eye.

While the government has stated that previous medical reports showed no condition requiring immediate treatment, the court order allows Khan access to a medical panel that includes his personal physician.
PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari described the ruling as a 'new ray of hope,' though the party still plans a nationwide march on September 27 to demand his release and speedy hearings.
The transfer is seen by some as a potential first step toward easing tensions between Khan's party and Pakistan's military establishment, which have been at odds since his 2022 ouster.
caption:
Jailed former PM Imran Khan has been moved to a hospital in Islamabad following a Supreme Court order.

Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was transferred from Adiala Jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad early Friday morning for a medical examination.

The move follows a Supreme Court order issued this week, requiring authorities to transfer the 73-year-old former leader within 48 hours.

Khan's party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), and his lawyers claim his health has deteriorated during his imprisonment since August 2023, specifically citing significant vision loss in his right eye.

While the government has stated that previous medical reports showed no condition requiring immediate treatment, the court order allows Khan access to a medical panel that includes his personal physician.

PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari described the ruling as a 'new ray of hope,' though the party still plans a nationwide march on September 27 to demand his release and speedy hearings.

The transfer is seen by some as a potential first step toward easing tensions between Khan's party and Pakistan's military establishment, which have been at odds since his 2022 ouster.
